commons.title: Ceramic Master in his garage working on handmade maltese souvenirs - traditional maltese balconies (or gallarija).jpg
commons.description: Ceramic Worker in his workshop between his handmade typical maltese souvenirs - traditional maltese balconies (or gallarija) as Malta is well-known for its beautiful balconies, which are a staple feature of the island’s architecture. Maltese balconies are believed to have originated in the 16th century, during the period of Ottoman rule. During this time, many buildings in Malta were constructed with large projecting balconies that served as a sunshade and a place to socialize. These early Maltese balconies were often ornate, with intricate metalwork and colorful tiles. Nowadays is becoming rare in reality and only some ceramic masters knows and representing this traditional example of culture and craft.
commons.editorial_reason: Explicitly identifies Maltese ceramic craft and souvenirs, visibly showing the artisan's workshop and objects.

commons.title: Fisherman repairing parit (or nett) in old way in the village of Marsaxlokk. Old traditional and typical trade.jpg
commons.description: That's (parit) tread nett. This nett can be used for any type of fish passing from the bottom of the sea. The world parit comes from the Italian world parete, which means wall. The parit is been putting in place at the evening and gett back in the early morning normally. It's like you putt a wall of nett for nearly 8 hours and than at the morning you can see who tried to pass from that wall of nett (parit). Old traditions still alive in colorful fishermen village Marsaxlokk
commons.editorial_reason: Identifies a traditional Maltese fisherman repairing a parit net, visibly showing the craft.
